This is issue 4527: a `static const` array declared inside a member function. The pixel and
mesh shaders in the report are restated here as a compute shader so that all three panes can
compile the same source; the construct is not stage-specific.

The two panes without an extra define fail. The failure is not a syntax error -- the shader
parses and generates code, and it is DXIL validation that rejects the result, naming the
array's mangled symbol as a global with no definition and its vector element type as
illegal. No object is produced, so nothing here reaches a runtime.

The panes built with -D CONTROL_NO_STATIC differ from the others in one token: the local array
loses `static`. That is one of the reporter's own workarounds. They compile, which is what
makes the failure specific to the construct rather than to the shader or the flags.

Local evidence uses the reporter's own pixel shader at ps_6_0 and mesh shader at ms_6_5, both
of which fail the same way; Compiler Explorer runs Release builds and its oldest DXC is
1.6.2112, so it corroborates current behaviour rather than dating it.
